objective: Native networks of every law are decided in polynomial time (NATIVE-HARDNESS-20261024-001), but emergent information is a count of witnesses. Ask which laws make native counting tractable. Hypothesis under test: for symmetric three-place relations, gluing topologically (SURFACE-GLUING-20261024-001A) is the same as being a generalized Fibonacci gate (Cai, Lu and Xia), so the four topological knots count in polynomial time while every other knot is #P-hard given the Holant dichotomies; and without pins, not-all-equal worlds count like an Ising model, easy on the sphere, with each handle multiplying the cost. Nearest known work: Holant dichotomies (Cai, Lu and Xia 2009; Cai, Huang and Lu 2012; Backens 2018), Fibonacci gates, and the Kac-Ward and Kasteleyn determinants. Standalone value: the identification of topological gluing with tractable counting, and the cost of counting read against the genus of the network's surface.
status: Complete 2026-10-24: counting what emerges natively. Topological gluing is the generalized Fibonacci-gate recurrence f0 f2 + f1 f3 = f1^2 + f2^2, so the four topological knots count every native network by closed formulas while the other 30 are #P-hard to count given Backens's dichotomy: emergence is countable exactly when it is topological. Closed not-all-equal worlds are an antiferromagnetic Ising model (e^(2b) = 1/2), a determinant on the sphere. Next: approximate counting, deferred to the owner.
title: Counting what emerges natively
